newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lederer to take over as D.Babcock CEO.
newsitem.headline: Lederer to take over as D.Babcock CEO.

text.p: Klaus Lederer, head of ITT Automotive Europe, will become chief executive of German engineering group Deutsche Babcock AG, replacing outgoing CEO Heyo Schmiedeknecht, the company said on Monday.
Deutsche Babcock said in a statement that the supervisory board had accepted Schmiedeknecht's resignation.
The company also announced it slumped to a big loss in its 1995/96 business year and posted negative cash flow.
Schmiedeknecht's departure had been flagged in the German press over the weekend. At the helm since 1990, he had come under fire for buying up companies which are now making losses.

Deutsche Babcock gave no reason in a regulatory statement for Schmiedeknecht's resignation, which comes as the company is embarking on a restructuring programme to refocus on core businesses and pare peripheral activities.

But it said that Lederer, 48, who has also been worldwide general manager of U.S. ITT Automotive Corporation, would bring an international dimension to Deutsche Babcock's business when he takes over at the end of January.
The company also said that, in the year to September 30, 1996, Deutsche Babcock slid to a group net loss of 434 million marks after a 46 million mark profit.
Group sales rose to 8.7 billion marks from 8.3 billion, but incoming orders were down to 8.4 billion from 9.8 billion.
Group cash flow plunged to a negative 279 million marks after a positive 251 million marks the year before.
